title: Intonational variation in urban dialects of English spoken in the British Isles
abstract: The production of prosody is subject to a multitude of factors: dialect, speaking style, discourse structure, syntax, the words spoken, segmental phonetic structure, speaker habit, gender, age and social background. This paper presents evidence for intonational variation in dialects of English spoken in the British Isles, drawing on the IViE (Intonational Variation in English) corpus of nine urban dialects. It discusses (1) variation conditioned by dialect and (2) variation across speakers of a single dialect, covering both phonetic realization (truncation vs. compression) and phonological structure (nuclear accent choice) of pitch accents.
